answers: Amy Schumer took the long way around to announce she's pregnant with husband Chris Fischer. The comedian and actress broke her baby news Monday on the Instagram stories of friend and journalist Jessica Yellin, the AP reports. Yellin, of the site NewsNotNoise.org, showed at the end of a list of Schumer's recommended congressional and gubernatorial candidates the line: "I'm pregnant-Amy Schumer." Schumer had teased the announcement on her own Instagram page, captioning a photo of hers and Fischer's heads atop Prince Harry's and Meghan Markle's bodies, "About to announce some exciting news on @jessicayellin insta page. Please follow her for up to the minute #newsnotnoise she breaks down what’s really going on. She agreed to post a lil noise today for me! Follow her and VOTE!!" "We are 15 days out from the midterms and there is a lot going on," Yellin explained before going into Schumer's "lengthy" list of recommendations, per Bustle. "I wanted to share some news from our community. Maybe it's noise, but it's happy noise," Yellin continued. "These are the recommendations of Amy Schumer, one of the most consistent and early supporters of #NewsNotNoise. Now, read all the way to the bottom. You'll see there's some news down there. Congratulations, Amy." Schumer is known for her liberal politics: She was recently arrested protesting the confirmation of Judge Brett Kavanaugh to the US Supreme Court. The 37-year-old married Fischer, a chef, in February. (Here's why Schumer won't appear in any Super Bowl ads.)

In a separate but equally significant development, Schumer has announced that she is expecting her first child. She shared the news through a strategic partnership with journalist Jessica Yellin, who runs the #NewsNotNoise campaign aimed at educating the public about political terminology and issues. Schumer directed her followers to Yellin’s Instagram page, where the news was revealed as part of a broader effort to encourage voter participation in the upcoming midterm elections. The announcement was accompanied by a humorous photo of Schumer and her husband, Chris Fischer, photoshopped onto the bodies of Meghan Markle and Prince Harry, who are also expecting their first child. Schumer used the opportunity to remind her followers of the importance of voting, leveraging her celebrity status to promote civic engagement.

Schumer has long been an active voice in political and social causes. She has been a vocal advocate for gun control, supported the transgender community, and taken a stand against the Trump administration’s policies. Earlier this month, she was reportedly detained and arrested for protesting Brett Kavanaugh’s Supreme Court nomination. Her commitment to social justice and political activism is evident in her actions, and her recent decisions—whether it be refusing to participate in Super Bowl ads or using her platform to promote voter turnout—reflect her ongoing dedication to these causes. By combining personal news with political messaging, Schumer continues to use her influence to raise awareness and inspire action.
